articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness of Braids with High Optical Coverage
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The shielding effectiveness of the braid of a coaxial cable is usually defined with the concept of transfer impedance and transfer admittance. The transfer impedance characterizes the diffusion of the tangential component of the disturbing electric field through the conducting material. For braided cables, this transfer impedance includes also a transfer inductance corresponding to penetration of the tangential component of the magnetic field through the openings distributed along the braid. Furthermore, a transfer capacitance has to be introduced to take into account the penetration of the normal component of the electric field.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Topology: A Formal Approach to the Analysis and Design of Complex Electronic Systems
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper summarizes several of the concepts included in the new and expanding subject of electromagnetic topology. Beginning with the elementary concepts of volumes and boundary surfaces, these entities are specialized to layers and shields, and sublayers and subshields, and also associated with equivalent graphs. Next one defines a set of indices associated with the various levels of topological decomposition. The general supermatrix equation describing electromagnetic propagation is partitioned according to these indices. The partitioned equation leads to useful approximate solutions which can be used to bound signals, relate the performance of the system to its parts, and allocate shielding to various subshields so that a system of interest can be protected against various electromagnetic environments.

articleTitle: A Probabilistic Approach to Wire Coupling Interference Prediction
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Unintentional electromagnetic coupling between wires in cable bundles (crosstalk) can be an important consideration in determining the electromagnetic compatibility of a system. In many cases, crosstalk can be considerably more important than other modes of interference coupling, e.g., antenna-to-antenna.

articleTitle: The Intrasystem EMC Problem and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The problem of designing a system such as an aircraft, satellite, or missile, and have it function properly without any electromagnetic interference (EMI) is becoming more and more difficult. This difficulty is partly due to the present day capability of analyzing and predicting a systems' EM status throughout its design stages and through its many modifications once the system is fielded. A portion of the analysis and prediction problem is caused by the rapid changing of other technologies (e.g. the advent of microelectronics, spread spectrum techniques, adaptive arrays, composite materials, etc.), partly by the sheer complexity of the systems caused by the increase in the number of emitters and receptors of EM energy that are crowded into smaller spaces and the lack of measurement data especially at the component level. This paper investigates a new direction for analyzing the EMC of a system by applying the probabilistic modeling approach of reliability theory to compatibility.

articleTitle: The Canadian Field Trials of a Computer Assisted Land-Mobile Licensing System
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The progress made by the Canadian Department of Communications in the development of a computer-assisted Land-Mobile licensing system have been previously reported in the literature [1,2,3]. The most significant step in this development consisted of the field trials conducted in the city of Montreal during 1979.

articleTitle: Measurement of Fluctuational Noise Characteristics in the Presence of Impulsive Interference
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Electromagnetic environment due to natural or man-made radiation may be somewhat complicated taking into consideration the structure of electromagnetic field as a random process. Widely encountered class of random radio interference making the electromagnetic environment rather complicated is an additive mixture of low power fluctuational background noise and the sequence of powerful pulses with random distribution in time. Typical example of this kind of random process having natural origin is the atmospheric noise field particularly withnin very low frequency band. The present report is an effort to estimate expected errors in measurement of spectrum density or the total intensity of low power fluctuational process in the presence of random sequence of powerful pulses, the effect of which is eliminated by interrupting the reception during the time equal or greater than the action time of the pulses.

articleTitle: Intrasystem EMC Testing-A New Concept: System Constituents
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Functional operation of a system, unperturbed by intrasystem interference, cannot be guarranteed merely by analysis or by testing its subsystems before integration. That makes the overall system EMC test essential. Such a test has to cover all the system's operational states combinations, which may amount to an order of 10<sup>5</sup> to 10<sup>6</sup> measurements in combat systems. In addition, safety margins have to be assured, in order to account for the spread in the repeatability of disturbance phenomenae from time to time and between units, particularly when transient signals are considered. Such a margin is called for by MIL–E–60510 and requires the insertion of special sensors into sensitive points in the system.

articleTitle: Using Macromodels to Compare RFI in Bipolar and FET-Bipolar Operational Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Macromodels containing two transistors are used to predict how AM modulated RF signals with RF carrier frequencies in the .05 to 100 MHz range are demodulated in µA741 bipolar and LF355 JFET-bipolar operational amplifiers (op amps) to cause undesired low frequency responses related to the modulation envelope of the RF signals. A comparison of predicted RFI results indicates that parasitic substrate capacitance effects are more important in bipolar op amps than in JFET-bipolar op amps. The predictions also suggest that demodulation RFI effects in the LF355 JFET-bipolar op amp may be lower than in the μA741 bipolar op amp.

articleTitle: Power Flux Density in the near Field of TV Transmitting Antennas
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In order to ensure both the safety of the personnel working within the proximity of high power sources of electromagnetic fields as well as for the protection of the biosphere it is necessary to know about the distribution and value of the electromagnetic field strength or power flux density. In the paper a method has been described for determining the values of power flux density generated by a TV antenna built of standard antenna panels suspended on a vertical mast. Assuming the omnidirectional radiation pattern, formulae for the electric field strength and for the power flux density in the near field of an antenna consisting of N arbitrarily excited but equally spaced panels, have been derived. On the basis of these formulae a computer programme in two versions (first in FORTRAN IV and second in FORTRAN 1900) has been written. The programme makes possible the calculation of power flux density at any distance from the antenna and at any height above the ground level. Computer calculations have been compared with the results of measurements carried out at the TV broadcasting station on Święty Krzyż.

articleTitle: Operation of a Low-Power Spread-Spectrum System in a Strong-Interference Environment
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: There is an increasing need to provide low data rate communication capability in a strong interference environment. This paper considers the use of spread-spectrum techniques for this application. For purposes of illustration, operation in the UHF television band is considered. Bounds on the transmitted power and bandwidth of the spread-spectrum signal are determined such that a desired error rate can be achieved without interfering with nearby TV receivers. This is done for both direct sequence and frequency hopped spread spectrum systems. It is concluded that the operation of a direct sequence system under these conditions is marginal, but that an appropriately designed frequency-hopped system could provide quite satisfactory operation and is currently feasible to implement.

articleTitle: Computer Model and Impulse Current Injections for Optimum NEMP Protection of Cables
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A step by step procedure combining analytical methods and simplified laboratory testing is proposed for the study of cable protection against NEMP. The three steps of the method are: development of a cable coupling model, surface transfer impedance measurements by impulse current injections and EMP simulation on long cables by impulse current injections in the sheath. The second step is particularly important when the theory cannot take into account saturation effects in ferromagnetic sheaths. The third step represents a practical verification on long cables of the model proposed in the first step. This procedure was applied with good results to aerial cables proving the validity of the computer model.

articleTitle: EMP Coupling to Extensive Systems
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Approximations are developed for the interaction of plane em waves with a conducting ground, and for point injection responses of ground laid cables, the latter being extended to distributed injection responses. The wave results are shown to be in agreement with numerical solutions and the injection responses are shown to be consistent with experimental results.

articleTitle: Recent Developments in Electromagnetic Field Coupling to Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In determining the behavior of a complicated electrical system subjected to an external stimulus (lightning, EMP, etc.), it is useful to employ various transmission line models for calculating how electromagnetic energy distributes itself within the system. Over the past few years, a number of computer codes have been developed for such analysis. These range from relatively simple, single wire transmission line calculations, to general multi conductor transmission line network models.

articleTitle: On the Agreement of Two Methods of Construction of Stochastic Models of Cumulative Interference-Processes
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The Report treats a construction of a cumulative process of man-made radio interference by a method which envisages a synthesis of successions of elementary pulses from individual sources. Different forms of location of these sources in space are considered, Effects of interference-suppression measures on a cumulative interference process are taken into account. The results of this interference-process construction are compared with experimental characteristics of probability distribution of envelopes (APD) presented in works of Middleton, Spaulding, Matheson.

articleTitle: Low Tension Power Line as a Fast Digital Data Transmission Channel
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In a modern building, many functions are automatically controlled, as for example air conditioning, lighting, supervision and access control, burglar and fire alarms, etc. Such automation systems require reliable transmission of data and command signals within the whole building. Since power wiring is already available in every room, it seems logical to investigate whether it could also be used as a communication network. In what follows, the typical characteristics of low voltage (consumer) power distribution networks are discussed from the point of view of their possible use as a transmission medium. Generally, it is found that the mains supply constitutes an adverse environment for conventional types of communication. A special modulation technique by which the HF signal spectrum is spread over a large frequency band is therefore proposed.

articleTitle: Effect of Ground Connection on the Coupling of Disturbing Signals to a Coaxial Line
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: To provide transmission of informations between various electronic equipments, coaxial cables or screened lines are used. For example, in telecommunication buildings, the length of these lines can be 10 m to 100 m. It is then of interest to evaluate the influence of the position and of the value of the impedance of the ground connections on the coupling of disturbing signals to cables.

articleTitle: A New Generation of Anechoic Chambers
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: An R.F. Anechoic Chamber is a test and evaluation facility which is designed to provide a constant and predictable environment for the performance of electromagnetic wave propogation measurements.

articleTitle: Some Uses of Electrolytic Cells in the Measurement of Electromagnetic Interference
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In the study of ’man made‘ and naturally occurring E.M.I., the latter due predominantly to world-wide lightning discharges, detailed study of the fundamental mechanisms has been preceded by the acquisition of long-term data usually sampled in some form and presented in terms of one or more of the conventional statistical moments<sup>[1]</sup> Several practical schemes<sup>[</sup><sup>1,</sup><sup>2,3]</sup> have been proposed in the past three decades based largely on digital techniques with all the attendant advantages in data handling currently available.

articleTitle: Computer Programs for Linear and Planar Arrays of Thin-Wire Dipoles
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Two user-oriented computer programs for arrays of thin-wire dipoles are described. The first involves a large linear array of thin-wire dipoles parallel to a perfectly conducting ground plane. The second involves a planar array of thin-wire dipoles parallel to a perfectly conducting ground plane. Various Toeplitz properties are used in efficient algorithms. Linear arrays of over a thousand elements and planar arrays of several hundred elements may be treated. The computer programs permit (a) analysis of the linear array with deterministic excitation and (b) analysis of the planar array with random or deterministic excitation.

articleTitle: Coupling of Fast Transients from Power Supply Lines into Coaxial Lines: Experimental and Theoretical Results
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The problem to be discussed in this paper has been studied in connection with signal transmission in a digital loop communication system [1]. We had to investigate how to predict disturbances caused by fast transients that are present on nearby power supply lines. The aim of our work was not so much to get precise quantitative results, but to understand qualitatively the coupling mechanisms and effects, and to estimate the maximum possible coupling for practical worst case situations. We tried to simplify the theoretical models as much as possible, as long as they still allowed us to understand the principal effects.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Emission from Accelerators and Electron Beams
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The electromagnetic fields in the immediate vicinity of the Experimental Test Accelerator (ETA) at the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) have been characterized. Various EM sensors that cover the frequency band from the very low frequencies up into the GHz region have been used. In this paper the experimental set-up and the measured data are presented.

articleTitle: Effects of Resistive Plugs in Suppressing Ignition Noise
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper describes the effects of the resistive plugs in suppressing ignition noise. The level of ignition currents which flow through the plug body is analyzed by making use of Rompe-Weizel formula for the spark resistance. Fron the analysis, suppression improvements of Shepherd's proposed filter plugs are discussed.

articleTitle: A Cable Coupling Code
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: An algorithm for computing the coupling of transient electromagnetic pulses to buried shielded cables has been rigorously developed for earth-return conduction effects of lightning discharges, EMP, or other interference sources. The buried cable is modeled as a straight horizontal coaxial transmission line of finite length with an inner shield and an outer armor, temrinated in typical communication-equipment load impedances. The general case is considered in which the outermost conductor is not necessary in perfect contact with the conducting earth, but has a contact impedance with the earth, as in cables with an outer dielectric covering for corrosion or water protection. The results are displayed as 3-dimensional relief maps of the time histories of the induced voltage or current magnitudes along the length of the cable. Tables of the results and graphs of the output as a function of time at any location along the cable are also produced.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of High-Speed Digital Data Transmission Circuits and Analog Transmission Circuits in Local Cables
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The problems of Electromagnetic Compatibility of data transmission circuits, wires used for high-frequency telephone transmission systems and for voice transmission in cables of Local Telephone Networks are considered.

articleTitle: A New Probe for High Efficiency Coupling
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper describes a highly efficient broadband cable induction probe that can be designed for optimum voltage/current coupling or maximum power transfer. This unique probe can be used as either a "receptor" in conjunction with a sensitive noise measuring instrument or spectrum analyzer, or an "injector" in conjunction with a high level pulse or signal generator. The author discusses the new probe's development, including operational theory, design principles, physical configuration, electrical characteristics and its application to EMI testing. The paper provides the necessary analytical background to support the design and the test results that demonstrate the improved performance of the developed model.

articleTitle: Systems Generated Electromagnetic Pulse Coupling to Cables
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The exposure of a satellite to an exoatmospheric nuclear burst produces a systems generated electromagnetic pulse (SGEMP) in the satellite<sup>(1)</sup>. The x-rays and γ -rays generate emissions of photoelectrons, Compton electrons, and secondary electrons from surfaces of satellite materials, which produce photo-Compton currents in the space within and about the satellite structure<sup>(2,3)</sup>. These photo-Compton currents generate electric and magnetic fields which couple energy into the satellite electrical circuitry. There is potential concern that the coupled energy may, under some conditions, be sufficient to cause upset or damage in sensitive circuits, resulting in mission performance degradation.

articleTitle: Utilization of Network Theory for the Solution of EMP Interaction Problems and System Hardening
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper discusses the hardening of electronic systems against an external nuclear electromagnetic pulse (EMP) environment, based on a topological shielding approach. The concepts of shielding topology, interaction sequence diagrams and signal flow graphs are reviewed and illustrated, using a hypothetical ground-based system as an example.

articleTitle: Radio Interference: The Limiting Factor in Spectrum-Orbit Utilization
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Of all the achievements of space technology, the first and still the only one that has resulted in extensive commercial exploitation is that of communications through earth satellites. Today, communication satellites can provide services to anyone with access to a telephone or a television receiver.

articleTitle: Comparison between Experimental Measurements of the Electromagnetic Field Emitted by Lightning and Different Theoretical Models - Influence of the Upward Velocity of the Return Stroke
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In this paper, we present the principal characteristics of triggered and natural lightning strokes measured at St-Privat d'Allier. We compare the experimental results with the different theoretical models developed. In particular, we study the influence of return stroke velocity on E.M. field. This study forms part of the continuation of the research effort of the “St-Privat d'Allier Research Group”.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Experimental Investigations of Loading Effects Due to a Perfectly Conducting Rectangular Cylinder in a Transverse Electromagnetic Cell
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The study of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), that is the electric and biological system effects due to electromagnetic (EM) radiation and EM calibration, require accurate EM measurement techniques for defining the EM interference (EMI) characteristics. Thus, fully enclosed rectangular transverse electromagnetic (TEM) transmission lines with thin inner conductors are often used for generating standard known test fields. In all cases it is desirable that only the dominant TEM mode should propagate.

articleTitle: Analysis of Interference in Telecommunication Networks Caused by Power Generating Windmills
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In this paper some considerations are presented with respect to the interference caused by large-size wind energy conversion systems into radio communication systems. Using the scattering theory the effects of the dimensions of the wind energy conversion systems and the applied materials are shown. Furthermore the requirements imposed on radio communication systems are summarized.

articleTitle: On the Probability of Communication in Radio Systems
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Probability of communication /PC/ in analogue radio systems is defined with respect to objective criteria at the receiver input. Randomness of propagation and noise in radio channels is modeled by simple distributions. Probability of exeeding the RF protection-ratio is explicitely calculated in various situations. The case of two correlated signals/over weaknoise/ is next presented with a novel solution for Rayleigh-distributed signals /in Appendix/. When interference and noise are commensurate, upper-bound and lower-bound estimates of PC ore here determined. Some remarks ore adt1ed on communication-range concepts, as interrelated with PC.

articleTitle: Measurements of Strong Electromagnetic Fields in the Frequency Range from 0.1 to 300 MHz
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The paper presents some results of measurements of strong electromagnetic fields in the frequency range from 0.1 to 300 MHz carried out by National Radio Inspection in Poland. The levels of field intensity in the vicinity of such RF equipment as induction furnaces, welders, dryers, diathermies, radiotelephones and transmitters are given. The instruments and measurement methods used in investigations of strong electric and magnetic fields are also described. On the basis of comparision of safety regulations with results of field intensity measurements, evaluation of radiation hazards is presented.

articleTitle: Comparison between Calculated and Measured Attenuation of the Site Recommended by IEC for Radiation Measurements
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The IEC Publication 106 method to check the measuring site in the frequency range 30 to 1000 MHz has shown inconveniences of poor agreement between calculated and measured values. Since such inconveniences are considered to be due essentially to the non-re sonant standard radiating dipole, it is proposed to check the site with both transmitting and receiving dipoles tuned at the measuring frequency and to determine the insertion loss of the site, usually called "site attenuation". The attenuation values for the 3-metre-measurement site recommended by Publ. 106 are obtained under four different conditions, that is with the transmitting antenna set at a fixed height of 4 m and 2 m, and with the receiving antenna arranged to have the maximum field-intensity reading just be low 4 m and above 1 m. The experimental results are compared with the values calculated under the same above conditions by means of formulae derived both from the theory of mutual impedance between antennas and from the simpler calculus in far-field conditions. Aim of these comparisons is to deter mine under what condition a better agree ment occurs between calculated and measured values for the site suitability.

articleTitle: Mobile EMP-System with High Flexibility
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A mobile EMP-system was developed for the electro-magnetic-compatibility testing of electronic instruments. The system features a very high flexibility and is composed of small and light parts to facilitate transportation. Thanks to the very modular design it can be erected on-site in one day by one man. It is possible to get an uniform field strength of 50..400 kv/m (depending from the size of the antenna) in a volume of about 25..3 m<sup>3</sup> with this system. The time dependance of the field within the antenna was calculated by a computer program. The developed program considers the dimensions of the antenna, the generating and the load circuit. Additionally the voltage on the terminating resistor was calculated.

articleTitle: Safety Control Systems Interfered with by Electromagnetic Noise
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper deals with the importance of electromagnetic compatibility for safety engineering. An introduction to safety terms is given and concepts of control systems relevant to safety are presented. It is the intention to show that a safety proof for an electronic device is not only carried out completely by considering the 'failure mode effect and critical analysis' (FMECA), but also by the proof of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC).

articleTitle: Matrix Formulation of Electromagnetic-Compatibility Problems
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A matrix formulation of problems of electromagnetic compatibility of arbitrary electrodynamic systems is proposed. This formulation is based on representation of properties of radiation, scattering and susceptibility of such systems in the form of series expansions in vectorial spheroidal wave-harmonics. Expressions are given for basic parameters of electromagnetic compatibility in terms of a proposed matrix formulation. Methods of determination of values of matrix elements are considered.

articleTitle: Effect of Hard Limiting in a PN Spread-Spectrum System
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper shows that hard limiting in a spread-spectrum system causes narrowband intermodulation products. In the corresponding analysis, superposition of a wanted PN signal, white gaussian noise and one interferer at the input of the bandpass limiter is being considered. The interfering signal is either a narrowband or a PN coded signal. It is found that the amplitudes of the resulting narrowband intermodulation products are independent of the spread-spectrum processing gain and of the type of interference. A complete loss of the antijamming capability may thus result for certain signal-to-noise and signal-to-interference ratios.

articleTitle: The Assignment of Frequencies to a Transmitter Network in a Broadcast Band to Avoid Mutual Interference
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: If frequencies are to be chosen so that the spectrum is used efficiently it is essential to have some means of calculating field strengths with reasonable accuracy. This paper describes computer programs which have been written for this purpose. Terrain data banks enable ground profiles to be produced rapidly over long distances. In this way the mutual interference of a large network of transmitters can be assessed.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Immunity of TV-Receivers to AM, RF-Fields in the 3 to 30 MHZ Range, Including the Influence of Connected Cables
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The first part of this paper describes an immunity test method and results applied to 10 colour TV-sets (PAL, B/G, with coax input) in the frequency range of 3 to 30 MHz. The method is called "integral test method", because TV-sets as well as cables are exposed to the interference field, simulating real situations. A simple RFI suppression technique is also tested. The second part describes a "synthetic test method" which is simple to realize. Prom results of four different test methods applied to three TV-sets we conclude that the immunity of a TV-set is proportional to the open circuit voltage of an interference source, having 150 Ω internal impedance, whereby the interference source drives currents through the chassis. The interference power from this source is to be applied to the antenna cable shield and to the mains respectively. Results from the synthetic method are in good agreement with those from the integral method. On the other hand the irradiation of the TV-set only (in a stripline) or the injection of an interference voltage at the antenna input do not reproduce the worst interference conditions of a real situation.

articleTitle: RMS-to-Average Deviation Ratio for Interference and Atmospheric Noise
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Receivers that operate in an environment consisting of atmospheric noise and user interference exhibit a performance that differs from that in atmospheric noise alone. This difference results from the suppression of V<inf>d</inf>, defined as the rms-to-average envelope, when a strong carrier is present in the receiver bandwidth. This paper quantitatively describes the V<inf>d</inf> suppression effect.

articleTitle: On Establishing Limits for Radio Interference at Mains Terminals of Television Receivers over the Frequency Band above 1605 KHZ
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This Report presents the results of measurements of interference voltages at mains terminals of television receivers and of mains decoupling factors over the frequency band 0.15 to 30 MHz. The technique of measurement of mains decoupling factors is set forth; a selection of an artificial mains network type is substantiated. The inexpediency of establishing limits for symmetrical interference voltage over the frequency band 1.605 to 50 MHz is shown.

articleTitle: Lightning and NEMP Surges on Gas Arrestors. A Computation Procedure for the Transient Response
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper presents a computer-aided procedure to predict the transient response of gas arrestors, due to lightning or NEMP strokes. Calculated and experimental values of transient resposes are compared for different surge pulses.

articleTitle: EMC Testing of Automotive Electronic Control System
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Government regulated vehicular emissions control, gasoline mileage requirements, and safety considerations can only be met by means of sophisticated electronic control systems such as microcomputer engine control systems, electronic break systems, and air. cushion restraint systems using electro explosive devices. All such electronic control systems must be electromagnetically compatible with the often quite hostile on-board EM environment.

articleTitle: EMI Problems in the Design of New Telephone Switching Systems
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The evolution of telephone exchange system, wich has begun in the 60'S, has introduced considerable technological innovations in the traditional systems using electromechanical equipment. The introduction of digital integrated technologies in the switching networks for speech and data has consisted in the use of micro-circuits with medium to high switching rates wich had previously been used only in processing units of large computer centres. In experiences accumulated in the course of implementing and field testing "PROTEO" system prototypes (fig.1), made by Società Italiana Telecomunicazioni ITALTEL, we have found that the high switching frequencies and the size of row of cabinets have imposed a rational integration of EMC requirements with system technical specifications. In this paper the method adopted for the above mentioned integration is outlined. The method is supported by specific environment measurements and by simulation program for time domain signal analysis; his output as susceptibility limits for system working condition is shown.

articleTitle: Comparison of EMC Measuring Methods and PFI Limits
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: It is possible to determine several measurement parameters, so that EMC measurement results or RFI limit values can be compared. These parameters are related to various spurious emission kinds and physical quantities. Among the most important parameters, we can find the caracteristics of the measurement network, the measurement distance, as well as the display mode of the pulse spectra and the response of the quasi-peak detector.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Proposal for Radio Devices Immunity Measurement Methods
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Methods at present standardized for measuring immunity of radio devices are few, and apply to particular types of apparatus and particular limited frequen cy ranges. The standards known to the author are only those of IEC Publication 315-3 for AM radio receivers /l/, the BE 905 (U.K.) and the EIAJ CP 205/208 (Japan) for the external immunity of television receivers /2, 3/, the SAE J113a (U.S.A.) for vehicle components /4/,and the general purpose MIL STD 462 (U.S.A.) /5/. Particularly, for every type of immunity for audio (and video) frequency apparatus, CATV components, FM radio etc., no standards exist. In this paper an attempt is made to propose general purpose methods for all types of radio devices and electronic associated equipment. In some case proposed methods consist on an improve ment or a modification of the above mentioned methods or of other methods experimented by different peoples. To these authors is due the merit for their work.

articleTitle: The Influence of the Human Body on the Radiation Characteristics of Small Body-Mounted Antennas, Especially in the Resonance Region from 50 to 200 MHZ
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper deals with the problems of transmitting and receiving antennas operating very near to the human body (such as radio telemetry, walkie-talkie, etc.)· We will show that at frequencies near the body resonance it is worthy to consider the usual "antenna" not as a direct radiating element but as an excitation one which works on the reactive field, so that the induced currents on the body surface radiate the desired wave (transmitting case). Conversely one can detect the reactive field produced by the induced currents from the incident wave. Better radiation pattern and better gain can be reached with this new concept. Measurements are in satisfactory agreement with the computation. We used a computer program developed by Harrington and Mautz /1/, /2/ and extended by Bevensee /3/. We will review the method of calculation and introduce an interesting new interpretation of the equations.

articleTitle: Susceptibility Problems of Home Entertainment Electronic Devices
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: With the rapid growth of the number and power of HF radiation sources of various kinds, the susceptibility of home entertainment electronic devices to electromagnetic (EM) fields becomes one of the most significant factors of EMC. The home entertainment electronic equi pment of curr ent production is moistly neither intended nor designed to work in relatively high field strength EM environment, therefore these devices are not usable in the vicinity of an EM radiation source. As was shown before, the most troublesome interference is caused by HF voltages induced in power lines or/and low frequency (LF) stages of the home entertainment electronic devices. This paper presents some results of measurements concerning the susceptibility of LF stages of home entertainment electronic devices to EM fields in a wide frequency range. Two measurements for each type of the investi gated device were performed: first in its original s tate as obtained from the market and next after inserting proper low pass filters into the LF stages and mains cord lead. The filters were connected provisionally, as it was not possible to change the design of the device. By this simple means a significant decrease of susceptib ility (20 + 40 dB) has been achieved. One may suppose that similar filters and other simple protective means if introduced by the manufacturer at the design stage would result in an even higher improvement of home entertainment electronic equipment immunity.

articleTitle: A Frequency Domain NEMP Simulator for Tests on Scaled Models
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: We present NEMP-simulation facilities under construction for tests on scaled models which work in the frequency domain. The reasons for selecting this method of measurement are discussed and the structure and instrumentation of the simulation facilities are described.

articleTitle: Investigation and Control of Immunity of Receptors to Interference
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Questions are considered, which are connected with construction of a mathematical model of a receptor. It is assumed that interferences are affecting several inputs of a receptor simultaneously. A dependence of a response of a receptor upon the disturbances which affect it, is used as a model, Such conditions for selection of test signals are found out, under which the probability of a normal functioning of a receptor in the existing electromagnetic environment is not lower than the prescribed probability. The advantages of those procedures of control of immunity to interference are shown, which are based on methods of planning of an experiment.

articleTitle: A New Approach to Anechoic Chambers
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper describes a mathematical model for calculating electric field patterns, due to an elementary radiator, in screened rooms and ane-choic chambers of simple geometrical shapes. The discussion is not restricted to conventional chamber shapes and the possibility of using an elliptical chamber for EMC measurements in the VHF band is considered.

articleTitle: A Method for Determining Statistical Characteristics of SHF, UHF and VHF Interfering Signals over Long Distances in Land and Coastal Areas
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In assessing the EMC of radio systems the major problem is the possibility of abnormally high unwanted levels during the worst season (the worst month, according to CCIR) i.e. during the period when high levels are the most probable.

articleTitle: Practical Measures at a Water-Blumlein 500 kV EMP Generator and Its Oscilloscope Measurements
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The present work describes a 500 kV EMP test simulator designed for coupling the fast simulated exoatmospheric EMP transients into different antenna configurations generating field-strength of about 100 kV/m with risetimes of 2-3 ns as it is required in the NATO standard reference. Before going into physical and technical details we want to lay out the four commonly used HV-Pulse generating principles and their differences. These different principles are sketched out in Fig. 1-4

articleTitle: Some Results from using the Modified Ebers-Moll Model to Predict EMI in Active Filters
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Computer-aided analysis is used to predict electromagnetic interference (EMI) effects in active filters. A specific filter configuration is examined to determine its relative susceptibility to EMI upset. The active element for the filter is assumed to be the 741 operational amplifier (op amp). The electronic circuit analysis program SPICE2 is used to determine the behavior of the active filter. Filter output with EMI injected into the op amp(s) is compared to the output produced in the absence of EMI. Signal distortion is examined.

articleTitle: Field-Strength Measurements in the Vicinity of LF-, MF- and HF-Transmitting Aerials
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In the vicinity of LF-, MF- and HF-trans-mitting aerials guy wires as well as metallic components of buildings, fences etc. can cause secondary fields with different polarisation and phase in relation to the primary field. In general the resulting field will be elliptically polarized and, in particular cases, have linear or circular polarisation, respectively /1/.Field-strength measurements in such fields with temporarily varying orientation of the field-strength vector should not be carried out with common receiving equipment using single dipole- or loop aerials, because they pick up only one component of the three-dimensional field-strength vector. The omnidirectional receiving characteristic is not the only special feature of a field probe for use in the vicinity of a high power transmitter. It is moreover necessary to extend its display range up to some kilovolts per meter or amperes per meter, respectively. Such strong fields can cause heavy shielding problems for the measuring circuit, especially in cases when active components are applied. To avoid such problems the basic idea of the measuring concept presented here is that in places where people must be prohibited by law from illuminating their houses by means of RF energy it should be possible to find some microamperes for a meter readout. A basic field-strength measurement equipment is schematically shown in Fig.1. It consists of an electrical or magnetic antenna, a rectifying network, and a readout device.

articleTitle: Modeling of Impulse Noise Bursts
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Our purpose is to study the impulsive phenomena X (t), that can be described by the following model: <tex>$ x\left( t \right) = \sum\limits_{i = 0}^{N\left( t \right)} {Z\!\!\!\!\!{-}_i \left( t \right)} $</tex> Where N (t) defines the number of elementary pulses that are simultaneously present at the same moment t, and Z<inf>i</inf> (t), which is a random function, represents an elementary pulse. The index i represents the number of pulses that are simultaneously present. So, N (t) defines the impulsive structure of the impulsive noise X (t). We can remark that all impulsive noises don't necessarly admit such a structure. The impulsive structure can be defined by two mathematical models that don't supply the same analysis of the noise. But the general markovian case, that is obtained from the Kolmogorov equations, is a synthesis of the two precedent models and we obtain the general formulas of the characteristic function and the covariance of the interference. The asymptotic case supplies the stationary model, and we obtain the general spectrum of an impulsive noise that contains an impulsive structure.

articleTitle: Measurement and Application of Secondary Surge Arresters for the Purpose of NEMP Protection
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Secondary surge arresters are used on the secondary low voltage side of power transformers for 50, 60 and 400 Hz at different places in the low voltage installation, such as entry points at buildings (shields) and at equipment and load cabinets for power supplies and control lines.

articleTitle: The Problem of Spectrum Dehsity in the Vicinity of High Power UHF TV Antennas
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The paper deals with undesired radiation in the vicinity of TV transmitting antennas of the decimeter wave range. The problem is very -important from the point of view of widely understood natural environment protection. Antennas of this range usually have high power gain, above 13dB, which with a transmitter power of 40kW gives on equivalent radiated power of 1GW. Investigation is limited to the near field region because here great flux densities are encountered, especially when antennas are placed relatively low in relation to the surrounding terrain. An algorithm is given and results of computational analysis and of measurements of near-ground radiation of one of antenna types are shown. Methods of reducing unwanted radiation are also discussed.

articleTitle: On the Measurement of Hazardous EM Fields in Lossy Media using a Small Loop Antenna
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Analysis of a circular multiple-loaded loop antenna as a probe for measuring EM fields in biological media has been presented in the paper. An integral equation for the current in the loop has been formulated. The incident field, the kernel of the integral equation, and the current in the loop may be represented by Fourier series, therefore, a method of Fourier expansion has been selected to solve the integral equation. It has been shown that double or quadruple loaded loop antennae can be used to construct both the electric and the magnetic field probes for measurement of EM fields in a considerably greater range of frequencies than the probes employing single-loaded antennae. Beacause of the relatively greater dimensions of these antennae the voltages on their loads depend on both electric and magnetic components of the incident field. Application of a suitable correction filter makes it possible to separate the desired component.

articleTitle: Ground Effects in the Response of a Single-Wire Transmission Line Illuminated by an E.M.P.
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In this paper we take an interest in the ground effects on the linear characteristics of an overhead transmission line and on its response to an electromagnetic pulse (E.M.P.). We give the propagation constant on the line in the limits of quasi-T.E.M. approximation. We compare its values with the exact solution for a slow or fast mode. For an E.M.P., the presence of the imperfect ground limits a great deal the range of application of the quasi-T.E.M. approximation.

articleTitle: Characterization of Interference Caused by Household Apparatus
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The development of more and more complex electronic Systems working at low energy level results in a higher sensibility to a large range of interferences with a broad frequency spectrum (0 - 300 MHz). To improve the immunity of such installations working in a perturbed environment it is necessary to detect the interference and to determine its waveform, the statistics of its presence and, if possible, its origin. The present paper shows the waveform of certain typical perturbations with a broad frequency spectrum which may be encountered in the interference suppression process of household device.

articleTitle: Current Status of Determining EMI in Microelectronics
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The current status of determining EMI in microelectronics is reviewed. The review emphasizes how individual microelectronic circuits respond to conducted EMI signals. Also reviewed are methodologies for evaluating the behavior of electronic systems that results from EMI effects induced in microelectronic circuits within the electronic system.

articleTitle: EMC Computer Codes and the User: An Adaptive Symbiosis
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Powerful EMC codes such as IEMCAP provide a comprehensive and substantial output which requires careful examination by the user. By the creative addition of interactive computer graphics, a new symbiotic process is established between code and user which provides the user a better reaction time and a deeper appreciation of the modelling process, of the results, and of possible corrective measures. Output examples from a new code called Advanced Antenna-to-Antenna Coupling plus Graphics (AAPG) illustrate the dynamics of the process.

articleTitle: Estimation of NEMP-Induced Voltages in Coaxial Cables with the Help of Transfer Impedance
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: NEMP induced currents on the shield of coaxial cables cause a voltage in the center conductor. The knowledge of this induced voltage and of the coupled energy allows a correct choice of the protective devices needed. The paper presents a method providing an estimation of this induced voltage. The induced current in the shield depends on the following parameters: peak amplitude and rise time of the NEMP, electric properties of the ground, cable characteristics (type, length) and the network wherein the cable is used. An extensive analysis taking account of all these parameters would be required to know amplitude and wave shape of the current pulse. Once the shield current is known the induced voltage can be determined using the transfer impedance Z<inf>T</inf>. The calculation of Z<inf>T</inf> is difficult for braided shield cables and for cables with ferromagnetic shields (saturation effects). Much easier than the calculation is the measurement of Z<inf>T</inf> in the time and frequency domain. As results the transfer impedances Z<inf>T</inf> of various cables, measured with two different methods, will be presented. Finally the estimated voltages will be compared with the induced voltages measured in an NEMP simulator.

articleTitle: Disturbances of Signalling-Protective and Telecommunication Devices Caused by Diode- and Thyristor-Controlled Locomotives
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The interference on track circuits and on telecommunication devices depends upon the magnitude of traction current and upon harmonics content in that current. A calculation of interference level is affected by many factors of uncertainties, and in many cases it has been found necessary to provide measurements in order to define the electromagnetic compatibility level of locomotive power traction circuit and track and telecommunication circuits. This paper deals with measurements of the influence of traction current and its higher harmonics on track circuits, with measurements of equivalent psophometric current and with measurement of longitudinal and psophometric induœd voltage in the line-side telephone cable. The analysis of measurement results and their comparison with the ones gained by calculation are given, too.

articleTitle: The Evaluation of EMC Techniques for Sensitive Production Tests
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper presents the reduction of high external EMI up to very low levels of some microvolts in a broad frequency range (2 kHz to 3 MHz). The use of various EMI filters of a partly non-conventional design (because of uncommon frequency and voltage range up to some hundreds of kilovolts) and above all a careful EMC design with distributed suppression.

articleTitle: On Worst-Case Additive Interference for M-Ary Signalling and Correlation Receivers: Results for Representative Signal Sets
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Specification of the worst-case additive interference for M-ary signalling and receivers using pre-decision correlation is obtained. The interference is constrained by average power and peak amplitude upperbounds on its Fourier transform. In addition, no statistical description is assumed. The performance measure is a weighted (±1) sum of the correlations between the received corrupted-signal Fourier transform R<inf>m</inf>(f) and each member of the signal set Fourier transforms {S<inf>m</inf>(f)}. This measure also depends on the signal-present probability p. The worst-case interference function W<sup>o</sup>(f) is shown to have an average power equal to the average power uoperbound and is independent of p. This power level is achieved with W<sup>o</sup> as a clipped multiple of | ∑S<inf>m</inf>| that follows the phase of ∑S<inf>m</inf>(f). The clipping level is the peak amplitude upperbound. The worst-case performance is explicitly expressed in terms of W<sup>o</sup> Upper and lower bounds are also derived with respect to arbitrary signal sets. Additional bounds are obtained for the interference functions independent of the signal set magnitudes and/or phases. Examples for representative signalling schemes and filter/window functions are to be presented.

articleTitle: Heavily Magnetically Shielded Room for Measurements of Extremely Weak Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A magnetically shielded room was planned for PTB-Inst. Berlin +) to measure extremely weak magnetic fields by SQUID-magnetometers. The shielding effect extends from DC to GHz-fields. An optimized design in technological and economical aspects was found in a cubical shaped construction. The inner dimensions of the cube are 2.25 × 2.25 × 2.25 m<sup>3</sup>, the outer dimensions 4.6 × 4.6 × 4.6 m<sup>3</sup>. The inner shell is constructed of 15 mm welded copper plates followed by 6 concentric magnetic shells of Permalloy sheets with foam plastic spacing.

articleTitle: Optical Link for EMP and EMC Measurements
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The analog transmission optical link covers the frequency band from 120 c/s to 120 Mc/s with a dynamic range better than 45 dB (peak to peak signal/r.m.s. noise ratio) and a rise time shorter than 5 ns. The link is commonly used under external test site conditions.

articleTitle: Voice Communication System Performance in the Presence of Automotive Ignition Noise
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper reports on recent measurements of voice system performance in a controlled automotive ignition noise environment. At a quiet measurement site in the vicinity of Tucson, Arizona, various combinations of from 1 to 12 vehicles of various ages, types and manufacture were used to provide impulsive interference to four voice communication system types. These systems were SSB at 23 MHz, with a 10 kHz bandwidth, FM at 75 MHz with a 30 kHz bandwidth, AM at 300 MHz with a 30 kHz bandwidth, and FM/PCM system at 900 MHz with a 300 kHz bandwidth. The statistical characteristics (amplitude probability distribution of the received noise envelope and the average crossing rate characteristics) of the interference were measured simultaneously with the system performance. Two methods were used to measure system performance. An objective measurement using instrumentation termed VIAS (voice intelliqibility analysis system) was used which produces an intelligibility measure called articulation index (AI). In addition, a subjective method was used employing phonetically balanced word lists and a highly trained listener panel to obtain the articulation score (AS). One object of the measurements was to ascertain if a relationship exists between AI and AS for impulsive noise, and, indeed, quite good correlation was obtained for all four systems. The results of the system performance measurements and associated results are presented and discussed in detail in this paper.

articleTitle: A Wide Band Measuring System for Time Domain Measurements
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A time domain electric and magnetic fields measurements system is described. The field sensors, the integrator unit, the wide band transimpedance amplifier and the fiber optic link were developed and matched together to obtain a complete, user oriented, system. The system can be used to perform both transient and C.W. measurements. After a brief description of the system's antennas and electronics, some examples of measurements are reported. The system was used in measurements of transient fields generated by static electric discharge in satellite thermal blanket and in the analysis of transient fields generated by the ignition system of a car.

articleTitle: Computer Simulation of EMI Effects in a 7400 TTL NAND Gate
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Computer simulated results of sinusoidal interference in a 7400 TTL NAND gate integrated circuit are presented in this paper. The interference is impressed at the input, output, power line, and ground connections. Parameters are defined in order to characterize degradation in the voltage and current waveforms. These are plotted versus amplitude and/or frequency of the interferer. Results are also presented for pulsed interference.

articleTitle: Calculations of Current Induced in Long Conductors by Exo-Atmospheric EMP
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Results are presented of calculations of EMP induced currents in long conductors by horizontal and vertical EMP field components. Reflection of the field due to the presence of the ground surface is considered. The magnitude of current induced in a buried conductor is found to be much dependent upon the electrical characteristics of the ground. The time duration of the EMP is also important for the magnitude of current induced in a long conductor.

articleTitle: Radio Interference Experiences with A 750 kV Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In the high voltage range, even a small reduction of the insulation distance in the planning stage of a transmission line results in considerable economical savings. As a consequence, however, unwanted environmental effects may give rise to new requirements for the designer and operator. Transmission lines should therefore, be built and operated so that in their environment a./ undisturbed radio and television reception could be ensured, b./ under the transmission line the electric field intensities do not exceed a given value, c./ the audible noise remains below an acceptable level. In the present case, of the enviromental effects of transmission lines, the phenomenon of radio interference a special problem of densely populated areas, has been subject to examinations.

articleTitle: The Magnetic Field of Three—Phase Transformers and Bus-Bars at Considerable Distances
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The calculation of the low frequency (50 Hz) magnetic fields generated by three-phase transformers and bus-bars of distribution substations is necessary for a successful EMC-planning in hospitals and research institutes. These magnetic fields are especially critical because their shielding is very difficult and problematical. At the Institute of Electrical Power Systems at Vienna Technical University the magnetic fields of three-phase transformers and bus-bars were measured to develop a suitable model for field calculation. From these measurements we realised that the field configurations near the transformers and bus-bars are determined by details of the construction. However at considerable distances there are simple field configurations which depend only on the main dimensions. This is valid at distances farther than 3 to 5-fold of the main dimensions. Therefore three-phase transformers and bus-bars can be replaced by simple loops and coils. In general the magnetic fields are elliptical ones but if the dipole moments of these loops and coils are parallel the result of the superposition is a single-phase field. And thus the calculation of the magnetic field becomes very simple. In this paper, for example, we use a 1 MVA three-phase transformer loaded with rated current to show that the measured and calculated field configuration agree very closelywith each other.

articleTitle: Acquisition and Utilization of Channel Occupancy Data in the Shared Frequency Assignment Process
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The public demand for Land-Mobile Radio Service has resulted in an annual growth rate in the range of 10 to 15% in many countries in the last decade and market forecasts have indicated that a five to sevenfold increase in Land-Mobile Radio Stations should be anticipated in the last quarter of the century in North America.

articleTitle: ACAP: Antenna Coupling Analysis Program
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: ACAP has been developed to evaluate the, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of transmitting and receiving equipments installed on aircraft when the interferent situation is caused by coupling between their antennas. The external electromagnetic environment created by the antennas installed an the aircraft is simulated on the basis of the mathematical models of the fuselage shape and of the transmitters emissions. Theoretical models of the receivers sensitivities are used to control the EMC of susceptible equipments when located in such an environment. The program works in the frequency domain. The models, the methodology and applied techniques for the antenna-to-antenna electromagnetic analysis, including path loss around fuselage, are discussed. An optional possibility of analyzing interferent situation arising from intermodulation products is available in the program. Useful indications have been obtained from the ACAP results about the definition of transmitter and receiver EMC characteristics and about the choice of antenna locations on aircrafts. Actual results of an analyzed airplane are presented.

articleTitle: Options to Open-Field and Shielded Enclosure Electromagnetic Compatibility Measurements
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper discusses optional measurement techniques that are being investigated as potential alternatives to using open-field sites and conventional shielded enclosures for performing EMC measurements. Techniques discussed include: 1) low-Q underground or buried test chambers, 2) transverse electromagnetic (TEM) transmission line cells, and 3) reverberating or mode tuned/stirred enclosures.

articleTitle: The Connector Pin Voltage of a Shielded Cable Immersed in a Radiation Field
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In this paper we discuss the relation between cable shield design, radiation fields, and system susceptibility/emissivity. This discussion leads to the concept of Critical Transfer Impedance, from which connector pin voltages can be calculated. We show how plots of Critical Transfer Impedance can be made, knowing the amplitude of the radiation field and the susceptibility/emissivity thresholds for the system under test. We then show how Critical Transfer Impedance plots can be overlain on surface transfer impedance plots for cable shields, to determine the shield construction required to prevent system failure in the surrounding radiation field.

articleTitle: Compatibility of Graphic Data Input Tablets
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Graphic data input tablets are devices which track the position of a cursor or hand-held stylus on a measuring surface. Their operation involves either electromagnetic, electrostatic, magnetostrictive, resistive or acoustic principles. These devices are subject to, or may generate interference according to the principle of operation that is used. Shielding may not be practical without resorting to a Faraday cage. A newly developed concept of acoustic radar for use with graphic input tablets is described. It is not subject to and does not produce electromagnetic interference. An accurate measurement of position of a hand-held cursor is obtained by recording the time which elapses between transmission and reception of a transient acoustic wavefront. Performance and interference aspects of such a system are compared with those of conventional systems.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field and Oxygen Interaction in Biological Material
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The experimental proof is presented regarding the interaction of magnetic field and oxygen at high pressure /OHP/ in biological tissues.

articleTitle: Adequacy of Low-Frequency Crosstalk Prediction Models
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: A re-examination of traditional, low-frequency crosstalk prediction models is presented. From the exact solution of the transmission-line equations for a 3-conductor line it is shown that superimposing crosstalk contributions due to mutual inductance and mutual capacitance between the two circuits is valid for a sufficiently small frequency. The widely-held notion that one can superimpose the effects of both mutual and self elements (inductance and capacitance) is shown to be incorrect.

articleTitle: Coupling to Twisted-Pair Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The susceptibility of twisted-pair transmission lines to crosstalk is investigated. The twisted pair is modeled as a bifilar helix and the results for the response of a pair of untwisted wires to an incident field are adapted to the problem. The model extends previous results in which the twisted pair is characterized as an alternating set of loops lying in a single plane.

articleTitle: EMP Hardening of Systems
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: An approach to EMP hardening of systems, based on shield topology and multiple shields, is described. A fundamental postulate that a source is prevented from interacting with a system circuit by enclosing the circuit in an impervious barrier is developed to illustrate the effectiveness of certain hardening measures, the priority that should be given to shield compromises, and the allocation of hardening among nested shield surfaces.

articleTitle: Calculation and Measurement of Transfer Impedance of Cable Sheaths
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: An underground cable with a sheath-armour screening system is subject to two main types of disturbance, depending upon the configuration of the screening system. In the case of a braid configuration, or one with gaps in the screen, the main type is referred to as "transfer admittance", and characterises penetration by a radial electric field [1]. In the case of a system composed of homogeneous concentric tubes, the main type is referred to as "transfer impedance", and characterises penetration by an azimuthal magnetic field.

articleTitle: On Optimum Frequency and Power Assignment in Transmitter Networks
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The problem of optimum frequency and power assignment in a transmitter network is formulated in this paper, and an appropriate solution method is proposed. The method allows us to determine a frequency and power for each transmitter in the network So that the total power is minimized and all relevant constraints and requirements are fulfilled.

articleTitle: EMC Design of Printed Circuit Boards and Backplanes
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: This paper presents design of printed circuit boards (PCB's) and backplanes to reduce EMI emission and susceptibility. Most EMC approaches to control emission will also have a reduction is suspectibility. Several of the considerations are especially important for analog and logic mixes or high-speed logic.

articleTitle: External Interaction Problems Made Simple with the Singularity Expansion Method
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The coupling of electromagnetic energy into complex systems such as aircraft, satellites, and missiles is a very complicated process indeed. Nevertheless, it is of great practical importance to be able to estimate this coupling. Both natural lightning and the nuclear EMP are examples of electromagnetic environments that can cause failures on modern aerospace systems. In order to protect electronic systems onboard these systems it is necessary to understand how electromagnetic waves couple into the systems.

articleTitle: An Optical Fibre Link for Lightning Stroke Current Measurements
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In order to perform measurements of transient phenomena in high level electromagnetic environments (lightning stroke) a data transmission system using optical fibres has been developed. Beside, this system must also permit the remote control of auxiliary devices installed in the critical areas. As the transmission system is mainly intended for lightening current measurements, the security distance between the emitter and the receiver has been chosen to be of 200 meters. An optical cable composed of two mono-fibres is used for transmitting information over the above distance.

articleTitle: Transient Overvoltage Protection: The Implications of New Techniques
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Reliability problems can occur from the use of modern electronic devices without applying appropriate protection techniques or using incorrect installation procedures. Although surge arresters are effective in limiting overvoltages, a metal oxide varistor can provide a much lower clamping voltage if installation procedures are taken into consideration. Sparkover voltage measurements, with a specified time rise, measured arrester performance. The response of the arresters to a current impulse was investigated and lead effects were identified. Tests indicated that the metal oxide varistor, installed with short leads, provides low clamping voltage.

articleTitle: Calculation of Nonlinear Amplifiers with Single - and Multifrequency Input Signals
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: In 1968 Glazer /1 / advanced an idea to creats a cosmic power station which would convert sun light energy into microwave radiation and transmit it is the Earth with the help of phased arrays. As a phased array it was proposed to use series of a great number of nonlinear amplifiers coupled by means of waveguides with slot radiators, the distance between two adjacent amplifiers being equal to half the wave-length of fundamental mode with frequency Ω<inf>o</inf>, coming from a master oscillator. Due to nonlinearities harmonics of Ω<inf>o</inf> will always be present in such a circuit. In the present article some methods for decreasing the level of these harmonics will be investigated that were poorly studied befors. If harmonics level is minimized and the harmonics power is considerably lower than the power of fundamental mode, the series is said to work in a single-frequency regime. In general the fundamental mode may be suppressed due to the buildup of internal noise and single-frequency regime with some other frequency or multifrequency regime will be established in the circuit. So it is of importance to determine the parameters of the series that ensure the existance of the fundamental mode only. The distance between waveguide slots may change under the influence of certain factors, e.g. exposure to neat. The fundamental mode frequency at the input of the circuit must be changed accordingly. In other words parameters of amplifiers series must be selected in such a way that in the necessary frequency band the series amplify the fundamental mode only.

articleTitle: Rocket and Balloon Observations of Power Line Radiation over Japanese Islands
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Observation of the Power Line Radiation (PLR) has been requested to reveal the relationship between the PLR and VLF emission. The PLR intensity over Japanese islands was observed by 4 times of balloon and rocket experiments in 1978 and'79. By the results of balloon experiments for the mesurements of horizontal PLR distribution on the Pacific ocean at Sanriku Balloon Range, Tohoku, Japan, the horizontal attenuation rate of PLR is approximately 1.3 dB/100Km. By the results of rocket experiments for vertical PLR intensity profile over Kagoshima Rocket Range, Kyushu, Japan, the attenuation rate in the ionosphere is approximately 1.1 dB/100Km.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Method of Moments - GTD Technique for Computing Electromagnetic Coupling between Two Monopole Antennas on a Large Cylindrical Surface
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The purpose of this paper is two fold. First, the idea of a hybrid technique for combining the method of moments (MM) with the geometrical theory of diffraction (GTD) is extended to account for the mutual coupling between two monopole antennas on a large circular cylinder by means of curved surface wave diffraction. Second, the results of this technique are compared to those of an analysis program used by the United States Air Force which predicts electromagnetic coupling between aircraft antennas. The close agreement between the results of these two different analysis techniques serves to validate both computer programs.

articleTitle: A Methodology for EMC in Microelectronics
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Large scale integrated circuits (LSI) and very large scale integrated circuits are extensively used in many of today's electronic systems<sup>*</sup>, e.g. the microprocessor controlled automobile. However, little is known about these systems when immersed in an electromagnetic environment (EME). A procedure has been formulated to determine the impact of the EME, or electromagnetic interference (EMI), on systems which utilize microelectronics. The formulation reported upon investigates three major areas: performance criteria, the procedure used to assess system performance (the methodology) and the application of performance criteria and the methodology to determine the limitations of the procedure. The primary emphasis in this report will be on performance criteria.

articleTitle: General Characteristics of Impulsive Noise Caused by the Operation of a Switch
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
