abstract: Characteristics of impulsive noise generated in electrical circuits embodying an active switch are discussed. Relations enabling calculation of noise level are given, and measuring circuits and measurement results confirming the usefulness of the proposed method of analysis are presented.

articleTitle: New Results in the Development of Canonical and Quasi-Canonical EMI Probability Models
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Class A EMI probability models are further developed and their basic parametr structures analyzed, to provide general statistical structures applicable to essentially all (Class A) EMI situations. The concepts of canonical and quasi-canonical models are defined, in the context of analytical tractability, and the central rôle of the EMI scenario (e.g., source distributions, propagation law, waveform structures, etc.) in determining the explicit form of the pdf and APD is demonstrated. It is shown that a rayleigh distribution of received source envelopes (B̂<inf>oA</inf>) yields the exact (canonical) form. All others are quasi-canonical, which are the most common in applications. Moreover, these quasi-canonical forms remain invariant of the particular scenario involved, depending on only whether or not the pdf of B̂<inf>oA</inf> is quasi-rayleigh, or "super-rayleigh".

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Phenomena and Reliability of Electronic Equipment & Systems
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Reliability and safety planning of complex electronic systems is applied when severe requirements must be met and safety aspects are involved. Electromagnetic interference (EMI) effects are disturbances which can have an effect on safety and reliability of electronic systems and ultimately must be avoided. In this paper the EM phenomena will be considered as sources of disturbances and events causing failures in electronic systems. EMI and EMC reliability planning will be explained in connection with the tender, concept & planning, design & development phases of a product life cycle. The fundamental methods of EMI and EMC reliability planning are described: Compilation of EMI and EMC reliability requirements; Definition of system functional failures; Allocation of EMI and EMC reliability; System reliability analysis; Determination of the failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA); Component failure rates caused by EM phenomena; Selection of mathematical models and methods. In order to carry out a quantitative EMI and EMC reliability analysis the failure rates of components used must be obtained. Mathematical models are used for the calculation by introducing an additional parameter, in which the EMI and EMC effects are considered. This method is demonstrated for some typical electronic components and for a representative electronic circuit (regulated voltage supply).

articleTitle: Effects of Direct Sequence and Frequency Hopping Interference on FDM/FM Systems
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The results of an investigation of the manner in which undesired spread spectrum signals affect the performance of FDM/FM multichannel telephony transmissions are summarized. Equations and graphs that describe the interference noise power resulting from a co-channel direct sequence or frequency hopping signal are derived empirically from the observed data. The investigation was largely based on an extensive measurements program followed by data analyses and reduction.

articleTitle: Influence of Low-Frequency Magnetic Field (LMF) on the Organism
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The aim of this investigation was to assess short term effects (T<1 hr.) of low-frequency magnetic fields (LMF) (B = 60 mT, F = 5 Hz - 50 Hz) on the living organism. Some special objective and subjective measurement methods were employed. In this way the influences caused by the magnetic field on the visual system could be determined. This is clear from the distinct flicker effects in visual perception and by changes in the visually evoked potentials of the subjects.

articleTitle: The TEM Measuring Line - A Critical Overview
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: The broadband TEM measuring line is a useful tool for testing the susceptibility of small devices (electronic or biological) to radiated electromagnetic (EM) energy and also for determining the EM radiation of small structures. It has, however, several inherent drawbacks which restrict its practical application. In particular, errors may occur by disregarding the physical limitations imposed on the intended behaviour of the line as a homogeneous field generator. The aim of this paper is to alert the user of measuring lines, who is supposed to be familiar with general line theory, to possible sources of error in the interpretation of test results.

articleTitle: Available Computer Programs Based on the Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 4th Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Zurich
abstract: Over the past ten years or so a number of general user-oriented computer programs or codes have been developed to solve certain problems in the area of electromagnetics - in particular, problems of electromagnetic compatibility. These programs are capable of providing a variety of useful output quantities with only simple input data requirements. Often it is not necessary that the user know the detailed theory of the method of analysis used or the analytical details that were involved in writing the program since these are all packaged within the computer program itself. The user-oriented programs focused on in this paper are based on the general method of functional analysis known as the method of moments, which was specialized for problems of electromagnetics by Harrington [1], [2], This method lends itself well to construction of useful and user-oriented codes for treating problems of both analysis and design. This paper briefly describes some of the most general of these together with certain of their antecedents, derivatives and related programs. The codes are grouped here by application area.
